html:
Costa Rica is a small country in southern Central America, between Nicaragua and Panama. It has been a separate republic since 1838 and is known as the most stable democracy in the region.

Under Spain it was a poor, remote province with few Native workers to exploit and no gold, so settlers mostly farmed their own land. After independence in 1821 it joined the Federal Republic of Central America and left in 1838.

In the 1800s coffee from the central valley, sold to Britain, made it prosperous. To reach the Caribbean, the American Minor Cooper Keith built a railway to Limón in the 1870s and 1880s, using workers from Jamaica among others, and planted bananas along it. His business became part of the United Fruit Company in 1899.

A short civil war in 1948 changed the country. Its winner, José Figueres Ferrer, abolished the army, and the money went to schools and health care instead. Elections have been held peacefully ever since. President Óscar Arias won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987 for a plan to end the wars in Central America. Since the 1980s Costa Rica has protected about a quarter of its land in parks and reserves, and nature tourism is a major industry.
sum: Costa Rica is a small country in southern Central America, between Nicaragua and Panama. It has been a separate republic since 1838 and is known as the most stable democracy in the region.
